guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why Texas is priced this aggressively. Our longer-run numbers identify its passing offense against UT San Antonio’s pass defense as the clearest advantage in the game. Texas reinforced that potential in its opener, producing 516 yards at 7.0 yards per play while Arch Manning threw for 305 yards and four touchdowns. We view that as supporting context rather than proof, but it shows the offense has multiple ways to create separation.

The more interesting part is what keeps us from finding value. UT San Antonio’s passing offense has a potentially favorable matchup against a Texas pass defense that grades less impressively in our numbers, and Texas has not been as dominant at consistently creating scoring opportunities as its overall offensive profile might suggest. Texas can still pull away, especially given its extended run of forcing turnovers at home, but our expectation is already aligned with what the market is asking. For us, those counterweights make this a pass rather than a reason to pay the current price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Texas’ passing game against the UT San Antonio secondary. Manning’s opener was supported by Ryan Wingo’s 121 receiving yards and Cam Coleman’s two touchdown catches, while Texas also returns four offensive-line starters from 2025. If that combination produces sustained efficiency and explosive completions, Texas has a clear path to separation. If UT San Antonio can limit those gains and force Texas to string together longer drives, the margin becomes harder to extend.

recent_game.fact: Texas opened the 2026 season with a 59-7 home win over Texas State on Sept. 5.
Texas generated 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas' running backs produced 156 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers—two fumbles and one interception—in the win over Texas State.

opponent_notes.fact: Texas and UTSA are scheduled to meet for the third time, with all three games played in Austin.
Texas defeated UTSA 41-20 in 2022 and 56-7 in 2024.
Against UTSA in 2024, Arch Manning recorded a 75-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo and a 67-yard touchdown run.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the 2026 opener against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a starter and 9-0 as a starter at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
In 13 starts during 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns while adding 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.
Manning took over for an injured Quinn Ewers against UTSA in 2024 and accounted for five touchdowns, including four passing and one rushing.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers produced 72 rushing yards on seven carries and caught three passes for 28 yards and a touchdown against Texas State.
Brown recorded 34 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Wide receiver Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and one touchdown against Texas State.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman caught three passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Texas returns four 2025 offensive-line starters: Trevor Goosby, Brandon Baker, Cole Hutson and Connor Robertson.
Texas added offensive linemen Laurence Seymore III, Melvin Siani and Dylan Sikorski through the transfer portal.
The listed Texas offensive linemen entered 2026 with a combined 226 games played and 114 starts.
Texas added tight end Michael Masunas from Michigan State; he had 19 receptions for 232 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: EDGE Colin Simmons led Texas in 2025 with 15.5 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, 15 pressures and three forced fumbles.
Simmons recorded one tackle, one-half tackle for loss, one quarterback hurry and one fumble recovery against Texas State.
Texas added defensive transfers Rasheem Biles, Markus Boswell, Justin Cryer, Darius Snow, Ian Geffrard and Zion Williams for 2026.

offensive_context.fact: Texas did not punt against Texas State, its first game without a punt since the 2023 game against Kansas.
Texas has not lost the turnover battle in 13 consecutive games.
Texas is 26-2 when scoring first since the beginning of the 2023 season.

defensive_context.fact: Texas has forced a turnover in 24 consecutive home games and in 36 of its last 37 games overall.
Texas has recorded 57 takeaways since the beginning of the 2024 season.
Texas recorded at least 40 sacks and 15 interceptions in both 2024 and 2025.

special_teams.fact: Mac Chiumento transferred to Texas from Florida State, Gianni Spetic transferred from Memphis and deep snapper Trey Dubuc transferred from New Mexico for the 2026 season.

series_context.fact: Texas leads the UTSA series 2-0, with wins of 41-20 in 2022 and 56-7 in 2024.

other_relevant.fact: Texas has won 10 consecutive home games.
Texas has won 21 consecutive home games against unranked opponents and is 21-1 in its last 22 games at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
Thirty-three players made their Texas debuts in the season-opening win over Texas State.
